entries.value: Château d’Esclans Whispering Angel 2024 is a pale, dry Côtes de Provence rosé led by Grenache, with Cinsault and Rolle. Pressed gently for a blush of colour, it blends bought fruit with estate fruit. It tastes of white peach, wild strawberry and citrus zest, with a light mineral finish. Its acidity meets raw tomato and its delicacy meets aioli, so it is our value bottle for the Creole Tomato Tostada and the Fish Bouillabaisse. We pour it at 45 to 48°F in a white wine glass, from the ice bucket. The name comes from two carved cherubs above the chapel altar, who seem to whisper.

entries.value: Loimer ‘Lois’ Grüner Veltliner 2022 is the fresh, everyday Grüner of an estate in Langenlois, the wine town of Austria’s Kamptal. The estate farms biodynamically, with no synthetic sprays or fertilisers, and this wine is fermented fully dry. Grüner Veltliner is Austria’s own white grape: here green apple, lime and white pepper with a green herbal note, light and crisp. Artichokes make many wines taste sweet or metallic, but Grüner holds its shape, and its pepper cuts the Parmesan creamed spinach and the Choron sauce, so it is our value bottle for the Eggs Sardou. We pour it at 45 to 48°F in a white wine glass.

entries.value: Stein ‘Weihwasser’ Riesling Feinherb 2023 comes from 60-year-old vines on steep slate near the old church in Alf, on the Mosel; Weihwasser means holy water. It ferments in large old casks and is finished feinherb, a grower’s word with no legal meaning, for wine just off dry. In the glass: Asian pear, lime and lychee with a salty lemon note, the sweetness held by crisp acidity. Sweetness cools spice and acidity lifts a dark roux, so it is our value bottle for the Seafood Gumbo and the Tuna Crudo. entries.value: Damien Laureau ‘L’Alliance’ Savennières 2022 is dry Chenin Blanc from Savennières, a small appellation of steep, dark schist slopes on the north bank of the Loire in Anjou. Poor rock and low yields give a wine of grip, fermented fully dry: quince, beeswax and toasted nuts, waxy and full, with Chenin’s firm acidity and a stony finish. Its nutty depth echoes the aged sherry and its acidity cuts the richness, so it is our value bottle for the Turtle Soup. We pour it cellar cool, 50 to 54°F, in a white Burgundy bowl, decanted briefly when young. Across the river, the Coteaux du Layon makes the same grape sweet.

entries.value: Trimbach Riesling Réserve 2020 is dry Riesling from a family house in Ribeauvillé, Alsace, the French side of the Rhine facing Germany. The house style is bone dry, made without new oak and released late, so it tastes of lime, green apple and white flowers, crisp and taut, with a stony, steely finish. entries.value: Kumeu River ‘Estate’ Chardonnay Auckland 2022 is blended from the winery’s own vineyards around Kumeu, west of Auckland on New Zealand’s North Island, on clay soils. It is made the Burgundian way, whole-bunch pressed, wild fermented in barrel and taken through full malolactic: lemon, white peach and hazelnut, gently creamy, with bright acidity and a fine, mineral finish. Its creaminess meets the miso butter and its acidity the sweet crab, so it is our value bottle for the Crab & Corn Omelette. We pour it at 50 to 54°F in a white Burgundy bowl, briefly in the ice bucket. A family from Dalmatia founded the winery in 1944.

entries.value: Cakebread Cellars Chardonnay Napa Valley 2023 comes from a family winery in Rutherford, in the heart of the Napa Valley, and it is a name many guests know and ask for. It is made the classic Napa way, with some oak, so it tastes of ripe pear and apple, with citrus and a little vanilla, round and polished, its fresh acidity keeping it balanced. That roundness suits butter, crab and cream, the richer plates of the house. We pour it at 50 to 54°F in a white Burgundy bowl or a large white wine glass, briefly in the ice bucket. The winery was founded in 1973.
